name: Monarchism in Brazil
summary: Brazilian monarchism seeks to restore a hereditary constitutional monarchy under the Orleans-Braganza Imperial House, modeled on the parliamentary empire of Pedro II. The Emperor would be a non-partisan head of state holding the moderating power, while a Prime Minister backed by an elected two-chamber Parliament governs. Its stated program is also socially conservative and Catholic-inflected, stressing the family, subsidiarity, strong armed forces and national reconciliation, and it leaves economic policy to elected governments.
scope: The contemporary mainstream of organized monarchism (the Vassouras line of Prince Bertrand and the Pro Monarquia campaign), based on its 'Propostas Basicas' platform approved in 1991 and revised in 2023, plus Wikipedia accounts of the movement and the Empire. It excludes the Petropolis branch (whose current head declared himself republican), the authoritarian Patrianovist monarchism of the 1930s, and the Tradition-Family-Property ideological milieu as such. Many economic and international statements are inferred because the platform deliberately defines no government program.

keyFigures.name: Pedro II of Brazil
keyFigures.role: Last emperor, whose parliamentary reign is the movement's model.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The platform is silent on health; subsidiarity (s1 B2) and acceptance of existing public services pull in opposite directions, so adherents are not clearly committed either way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed; the platform only wants better teacher pay (B2), and wage policy is left to the Prime Minister's government.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred from the conservative, subsidiarity-minded outlook; no economic program is stated because the platform leaves programs to the Prime Minister.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: subsidiarity and preference for private provision in education (B2) suggest wariness of state ownership, but nothing is stated.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the conservative-Catholic outlook and class-harmony emphasis; taxation is not discussed.

unions-good.rationale: The platform commits to free trade unionism under the ILO charter (B5), but does not say unions are good for society, so the endorsement is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not stated in the platform; inferred from its conservative, anti-class-struggle stance and the monarchist tradition of defending property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No stated view; neither Catholic social teaching nor conservatism points clearly one way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: Catholic care for the poor and the family-as-model language (C2) make outright cuts unlikely, though subsidiarity favours private help.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from collaboration between classes (C1-C2) rather than restructuring ownership; not discussed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from strong valuing of police and security forces (B3-B4); surveillance itself is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on family and Christian civilization (B1); drugs are not mentioned.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The platform asks for the broadest media freedom (B6) yet wants legal protection of honor and family morality, so adherents are split on restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: The Emperor is head of state, not government (intro, A3); the executive sits with a Prime Minister who needs Parliament's confidence, so bypassing gridlock by a strongman is not the model.

state-harmful.rationale: The platform builds a full state: Parliament, judiciary, Council of State, armed forces and police (A, B3-B4); it is plainly not anarchist.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents plausibly split between order-minded restriction and conservative gun rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: B3 and B4 call for valuing and supporting the armed forces, military police and civil police, with proper conditions and recognition.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the platform's defense of family morality as the foundation of Christian civilization (B1).

decide-locally.rationale: A7 keeps federalism and A8 expands municipal autonomy, so decisions move toward local levels, though the national Crown stays.

rehabilitation.rationale: No penal philosophy is stated; Christian outlook supports reform, order-minded outlook supports punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: B1 calls the family the mother cell of society and the foundation of Christian civilization, and C2 models monarchy itself on the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Follows from the Catholic doctrine the platform and its defenders link to monarchism (B1, s4) rather than from an explicit statement. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

abortion-legal.rationale: B1 asks for protecting the life of offspring and an anti-infanticide consciousness in every home; Catholic doctrine on this is firm.

more-religion-public.rationale: B1 names Christian civilization as the basis of society, and a prominent defender ties monarchism to Catholic doctrine (s4).

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents honor the 1888 abolition by Princess Isabel (s3) but the platform does not address present remedies, so views split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the family-centered Christian outlook in B1; the topic is not addressed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement frames the Crown as symbol of national unity and continuity with the Empire that assured Brazil's unity and greatness (C1).

gradual-change.rationale: The plan restores the 1824 Constitution with needed adaptations to present reality (A1) and keeps judicial and federal institutions (A5, A7).

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in the program; no clear shared view.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from the platform's national-unity focus (C1); no stated view.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from conservative, pro-market leanings; not in the platform.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from the patriotic framing of armed forces as guardians of the Nation and its international standing (B3).

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The sources say nothing on foreign policy beyond valuing the armed forces (B3); Catholic just-war thinking and sovereignty concerns leave adherents without a clear line.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on national unity and tradition; not addressed.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from conservative pro-development outlook; the platform is silent.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative skepticism of sweeping state programs.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No source treats technology; the movement's focus is institutional and moral, so no lean can be drawn.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative pro-development outlook.

revolution-justified.rationale: The platform insists the restoration campaign be conducted at a high level, aimed at ideas not people (C2), and modern monarchists seek a plebiscite; historic revolts (s2) failed and are not the program.

experts-over-public.rationale: A Council of State of eminent figures chosen by the Emperor (A6) gives experts an advisory role, but Parliament is elected by universal suffrage (A4).

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from conservative outlook and subsidiarity; not stated.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred; the platform proposes no ownership change.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative taxation views.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; hereditary continuity of family and Crown suggests dislike.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative, subsidiarity outlook.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic policy is explicitly left to the Prime Minister's government (intro), so the movement itself holds no tariff position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from subsidiarity and private-sector preference (B2).

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not discussed; incompatible with the platform's conventional order.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from conservative preference for existing institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Catholic social thought favors cooperation, but the platform uses free unions (B5) and an elected Parliament (A4).

one-party-rule.rationale: A4 and A3 establish a Parliament elected by universal suffrage and a Prime Minister with its confidence; C2 treats parties as legitimate participants in debate.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A1 and A2 call for restoring a hereditary monarchy under the Imperial House.

democracy-best.rationale: The proposed monarchy is parliamentary with universal-suffrage elections (A3-A4), though adherents argue the monarchy improves on republican democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: The model is representative parliamentarism (A3-A4); direct decisions are used only for plebiscites on new states (A7).

workers-councils.rationale: Incompatible with the bicameral elected Parliament in A4.

right-to-secede.rationale: C1 calls for national union around the heir of the emperors who secured Brazil's unity; A7 allows only new states made within the federation by plebiscite.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred from hereditary legitimacy (A2) and a Council of State drawn from eminent figures (A6), but 'natural' fitness is not stated.

political-violence-never.rationale: C2 asks for a campaign that does not target persons or parties; the absolute claim is inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; family-model peaceful language in C2.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic orientation of the movement (s4) and Christian civilization language (B1); no explicit church-state proposal.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic natural-law tradition shapes values, but the platform does not base law on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A5 protects an independent public judiciary and B3-B4 give defense and police to the state.

military-superiority.rationale: B3 stresses the armed forces' prestige and efficiency for Brazil's standing abroad, but superiority over rivals is not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: C1 calls on all Brazilians to unite, and the Imperial tradition included a multiethnic nation; not stated.

class-struggle-history.rationale: C1-C2 call for reconciliation of all Brazilians, forgetting divisions, on the family model.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative and hierarchical outlook.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The platform has no indigenous policy; Imperial-era tradition and present conservative views point in different directions.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative outlook.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nothing in the platform concerns supranational blocs; its focus is Brazil's own national unity (C1).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-civilization and duty-of-family emphasis (B1).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from family-as-model community (C2); not stated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic creation theology suggests mild agreement.

limit-population.rationale: B1 values the life of the offspring and the family; population limitation conflicts with it. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; clashes with conventional conservative views of progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from preference for institutional continuity (A1).

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic outlook suggests caution.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on human monarch and Parliament.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A technical privacy question absent from monarchist writings; order-minded and liberty-minded adherents would split.

restore-past-order.rationale: The program is itself a restoration of the 1824 constitutional order (A1), though adapted to current realities.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; the Prime Minister's program is left open (intro).

direct-action.rationale: The platform channels change through ideas and a plebiscite (C2, s4), not street action.

means-match-ends.rationale: C2 wants a campaign that reflects the harmony of the desired monarchy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly foreign to a program that restores a parliamentary state with a bicameral legislature and courts (A3-A5).

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; conflicts with conventional order.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative outlook.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist framing absent from the platform; the movement leaves economic organization to ordinary parliamentary politics (intro).

profit-exploitation.rationale: Contrary to the class-harmony view in C1-C2; not explicitly debated.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejects class struggle and rests on a parliament elected by all (A4, C2).

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative property views.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis; the program's class-harmony language (C2) implies rejection, though it is never addressed directly.

taxation-theft.rationale: The program assumes a functioning state financing forces, courts and teachers (A5, B2-B3).

harm-principle.rationale: B1 and B6 allow law to defend family and social morality, going beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: B1 treats the family as the basic unit; not stated against group rights.

conscription.rationale: B3 honors the armed forces as guardians of the Nation; conscription not addressed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Parliament elected by universal suffrage (A4) is the main check, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from national-family conception of the state (C2).

positive-liberty.rationale: Philosophical question not covered; adherents' emphasis on family and subsidiarity (B2) does not resolve it.

media-academia-power.rationale: B6 wants protection against media attacks on family morality, suggesting concern for media's influence; not stated about universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: C1 calls for unity of all Brazilians; not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: A4 elects Parliament by universal suffrage and A3 uses parliamentary confidence, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: B2 applies subsidiarity: family educates first and the state only completes what is needed.

national-rebirth.rationale: C1 calls for a union of living forces to overcome grave crises, but not for a radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Program defends national territory (B3) but not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Emperor rules within constitutional law and Parliament (A3), not through personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Slavery was abolished by Princess Isabel (s3) and nothing in the program restores bonded labor.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred from Christian civilization and Catholic natural law.

single-common-good.rationale: C1 urges a sacred union of Brazilian forces around one throne, implying one national good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not discussed in any source I opened; no inference from the Brazilian monarchist program is possible.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed in the monarchist sources; no basis for a lean.

revive-national-language.rationale: Portuguese is the established national language and revival is not an issue for the movement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the platform's picture of society as a family with a head (C2) and class collaboration; workplace votes are not discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: B2 says the state must develop the private school network and supplement it with public schools, which is close to vouchers. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative fiscal outlook.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred only from general conservative leanings; the platform says media freedom was broad under Pedro II (B6) but is silent on economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: C2 casts monarchy on the family model, with the sovereign as moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from national-unity framing; not stated.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign-policy detail the program never addresses; no clear lean.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from national-community framing.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative outlook.

class-collaboration.rationale: Sections C1-C2 of the platform call for the union of all Brazilians and setting aside divisions, which leans toward class harmony, but they say nothing specific about employers and workers as partners.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The whole program restores inherited institutions and symbols (A1, A2).

dominated-front.rationale: No monarchist source frames a front against Western powers; inferred as unlikely given conservative, Western-Christian self-image (B1).

workers-nation.rationale: The class-or-nation question is not posed in the program; C1-C2 national union leaves it open at best.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic tradition no longer holds this.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The imperial tradition ended slavery in 1888 (s3) and C1 unites all Brazilians; segregation has no place.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim; the platform's view of the state as shared national family under the Crown (C2) implies rejection.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-development conservatism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are absent from the platform; adherents plausibly split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; conspiratorial claims unlikely to be official.

proportional-representation.rationale: A4 sets universal-suffrage elections for both chambers without naming a system.

national-mission.rationale: The program is domestic (A-C); no mission to export a form of government is stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: A defender argues presidents think of the next election while a monarch is above party interests, and says Brazil has been unstable since 1889.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: B1 defends the life of offspring and family; Catholic doctrine opposes eugenics. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The platform praises the forces (B3-B4) but does not discuss accountability for past abuses; adherents likely split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program has the state also complete education (B2) and uphold family morality (B6).

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: C1 calls on all Brazilians to unite; the monarchy is idealized as a family.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from Christian dignity; hereditary monarchy complicates equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist dispute with no counterpart in monarchist thought.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from national-founding-narrative of Empire.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; single national law is implied by the unified Empire.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic orientation vs. 19th-century toleration.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a monarchist issue; Brazil's large livestock sector and Catholic custom suggest rejection, but nothing is stated.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: B2 stresses family educational authority and Christian civilization.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine unrelated to the platform; implausible for adherents.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents seek a plebiscite and a parliament with universal suffrage (A4, s4), though the Crown's legitimacy is also hereditary.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not in the platform; economic policy is left to government (intro).

population-transfer.rationale: C2 asks reconciliation of all Brazilians without hatreds or persecution of persons.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The platform backs armed forces and police (B3-B4), so an absolute rule is not clear.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Contrary to harmony message of C2; not addressed.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: C2 treats parties as part of debate; no stated view on banning.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-theory formulation not used in monarchist sources; with a hereditary head of state, adherents would not obviously accept it.

separated-powers.rationale: The plan has a bicameral legislature, a PM-led executive, an independent judiciary (A5) and the Emperor's moderating power (A3).

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed to class struggle and revolutionary politics (C1-C2).

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic-inspired concern, but not in the platform.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy with no Brazilian monarchist treatment.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: B5 respects free unionism; strike law is not addressed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; family-values outlook rejects population explanation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: C1 calls for unity but nothing links it to diversity; adherents plausibly split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to the platform's Emperor-appointed Council of State (A6) and elected Parliament (A4).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The platform stresses legal independence of judges (A5); emergency powers are not addressed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative outlook.

party-controls-media.rationale: B6 says media should have the broadest powers to inform and shape opinion, as under Pedro II.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization not discussed in the program.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No pay limit proposed; the platform keeps a conventional elected Parliament (A4).

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; PM depends on Parliament and Emperor's confidence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national unity under the Crown (C1); no source addresses supranational unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The current platform (A3) has a Prime Minister governing with parliamentary confidence, while the 1824 model it honours gave the Emperor executive and moderating power; the movement does not settle who should command the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Catholic orientation (s4).

clerical-rule.rationale: Government is by Emperor and Parliament (A3-A4), not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: B3 honors the armed forces as guardians of the Nation; class-based defeatism is at odds with C1.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: B6 asks for protection of family and social morality yet wide media freedom.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Re-election limits are not discussed; the head of state is hereditary and the PM depends on Parliament (A3).

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; A3 relies on parliamentary confidence instead.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The program praises the forces' role (B3) but says nothing on alliances; no clear lean.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; conflicts with property respect.

people-in-arms.rationale: B3-B4 rely on professional forces and police as reserves.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not a theme of the program; some Catholic-traditionalist writers say yes but the sources do not.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the platform even wants to raise teachers' pay (B2), so hostility to educated people is not evident.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from claim of Christian civilization (B1).

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic stance vs. order-minded outlook.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: B2 gives family primary duty for educating children.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic doctrine accepts evolution broadly while some conservatives dissent.

restrict-pornography.rationale: B6 asks for legal defense of family and social morality in media.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; Brazil's birthright citizenship is the baseline.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed in the program; Brazil's minority-language question is marginal for monarchists.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic majority outlook gives no clear lean on exemptions for minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity with tradition valued (B1); not addressed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International finance is not addressed; inferred as unlikely from conservative fiscal outlook.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A dependency-theory claim absent from monarchist sources; the platform seeks restoration of political institutions only.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The plan restores the 1824 constitution via plebiscite (A1, s4), not a new assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: B6 and A5 protect freedoms; not addressed on growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not discussed; Catholic charity and nationalist priorities pull opposite ways.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear arms are not mentioned; the platform values forces generally (B3).

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A2 makes the head of state hereditary in the Imperial House.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not in the platform; mild conservative inference only.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Brazil has no such territorial dispute; no source treats it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic social teaching; not stated in sources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A leftist debate that monarchist sources do not engage; adherents just reject Soviet communism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; no environmental regulatory position in the program.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances unmentioned; inferred as mildly favorable given emphasis on security (B3).

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed, and not a Brazilian monarchist concern.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Movement is tied to Catholic doctrine (s4); program wants Christian civilization (B1).

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A3 makes the Emperor head of state, not government, holding the moderating power above the Prime Minister (intro).

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: C1 stresses national unity; force not stated.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A7 keeps the federal system; special regimes are not addressed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Constitutional model with a ruler bound by Parliament (A3); divine descent not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design is left to the PM's government; the platform states no preference.

character-from-environment.rationale: An abstract theory-of-human-nature question not treated; family upbringing is emphasised (B1) but innate nature is also assumed in Catholic thought.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A defender stresses the monarch is subject to the laws (s4), and the model is constitutional (A1).

space-expansion.rationale: Not mentioned in any monarchist source.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Hereditary Crown, appointed Council of State (A6), and elected two-chamber Parliament (A4) mix elements.

leader-cult.rationale: The Emperor is a constitutional symbol; C2 focuses on ideas not persons.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court practice is not discussed; the family-protection language (B1) does not decide it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question outside monarchist concern.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; no Brazilian monarchist treatment.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist claims are not part of the program; Brazil has no such claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not a feature of Catholic monarchist writing; the sources say nothing about punishing religious exit.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to Brazilian monarchist tradition.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; no monarchist source discusses currency unions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions are irrelevant to the Brazilian program; no view stated.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the monarchist program is about national unity (C1) and federalism (A7).

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A diaspora-politics question that does not arise for Brazilian monarchism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis; the program's moral and religious framing (B1, C2) implies rejection though history theory is not discussed.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is absent from the program.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic policy is left to the PM (intro); no position stated.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: A5 secures judges' life tenure, irremovability and salary, to keep the judiciary independent.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditional family outlook (B1) as mildly opposed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is not part of the program; no source addresses it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: B5 adheres to the ILO charter; the rest is not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: A socialist concept not found in monarchist writings; no lean.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: C2 wants the campaign waged at a high level aimed at ideas.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A2 restores a hereditary monarchy and the Imperial House.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on the Empire's heritage (C1).

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage is not addressed; Brazil's own imperial history is not framed this way in the sources.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from B3 and C1 patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Brazilian quota policies are not discussed in the sources I opened; adherents plausibly split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not in the program; inferred opposed from conservative outlook.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A Marxist-debate question; conservative adherents would lean yes but nothing is stated.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not discussed; Brazil's own empire did not rule other regions beyond its borders in the sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: A dependency-theory prescription absent from monarchist sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis not addressed by monarchist sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on order, strong armed forces and stability, tempered by its parliamentary constitutionalism.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the platform; adherents are not united on the point.

indirect-election.rationale: The platform wants an elected two-chamber Parliament and a non-partisan hereditary head of state, not council-delegate selection of offices; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The platform does not address border plebiscites; adherents are not clearly committed either way.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The movement stresses the territorial unity inherited from the Empire and the Portuguese colonial legacy, so it would favour keeping inherited borders; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Simple self-sufficient living is not a program topic; an economics-neutral platform leaves it to individuals.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The platform is silent on settlement in Indigenous regions; inferred neutral given its call for national unity and its pro-armed-forces stance pulling opposite ways.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on national reconciliation and the historic imperial patrimony; spiritual language about the land is not explicit.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the platform's constitutional, rule-of-law framework and Catholic-inflected social conservatism; no stated position on killings of drug suspects.

close-ties-china.rationale: The platform deliberately defines no foreign economic programme and leaves such choices to elected governments.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the platform's defence of individual liberties under a constitutional monarchy; not stated in these terms.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the movement's constitutionalism and equality-before-the-law stance; not a stated plank.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The platform is Catholic-inflected but defines a constitutional state; the sources do not show a stand on denominational politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from the platform's socially conservative, tradition-valuing stance combined with acceptance of a modern state.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The platform is socially conservative and Catholic-inflected, but the sources do not state a position on divorce initiation, and adherents may differ.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on national reconciliation and strong armed forces, which suggest national control of strategic assets; not explicit.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The platform leaves economic policy to elected governments and is socially conservative; a conservative adherent would likely accept process-based justice of distribution, inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The platform deliberately defines no economic programme, so there is no stance on a transactions tax; neutral.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The platform does not address automation and has no economic programme, so neutral.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The platform is socially conservative and Catholic-inflected with no Marxist element; inferred that adherents reject the labour theory of value.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not a left movement, so the question does not directly apply; no stance documented, neutral.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: A hereditary constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament and a socially conservative platform is opposed to a communist-led socialist system.

missingStatements.text: The head of state should hold a neutral moderating power to arbitrate between the executive, legislative and judicial branches.
missingStatements.rationale: A3 of the platform assigns the moderating power to the Emperor as a defining feature of the restored monarchy, and the 1824 constitution created it as a separate branch.

missingStatements.text: Judges and prosecutors should hold life tenure and be irremovable so that they stay independent.
missingStatements.rationale: A5 of the platform keeps life tenure, irremovability and irreducible salaries for judges and prosecutors.

notes: The platform leaves government programs to the Prime Minister, so economic, international and many social answers are low-confidence inferences from its Catholic-conservative framing. The Petropolis branch and some adherents differ, and the 1930s Patrianovists were authoritarian. The Gazeta do Povo source was read through a summarizing fetch tool.
